program: E.C.H.O. care coordination and street outreach
what_they_offer: Village care coordinators connect residents, including people experiencing homelessness, to shelter, food, health and other services.
when_to_use: When an Oak Park resident needs help finding services (shelter, food, health and more) on a weekday and it is not a crisis.
who_is_eligible: Oak Park residents; referral from Police or Fire, walk-in at Village Hall, or direct contact
how_to_reach: 708-358-5640; echo@oak-park.us; Village Hall, 123 Madison St., Oak Park; https://www.oak-park.us/Community/Community-Services/E.C.H.O-Engaging-Community-for-Healthy-Outcomes
notes: Not a crisis service. Phone confirmed by team on 2026-10-03.

what_they_offer: Overnight emergency shelter in Oak Park.
when_to_use: When someone needs a bed tonight; arrange it through the Support Center or Street Outreach, since walk-ins are not accepted.
who_is_eligible: People experiencing homelessness; no walk-ins, intake through the Support Center or Street Outreach team
how_to_reach: 112 S. Humphrey Ave., Oak Park (intake via Support Center or 877-426-6515); https://www.housingforward.org/services/respond
notes: From the Street Outreach Card on the Village Resources for the Unhoused page. Shelter space is not guaranteed.

program: Suburban Cook County Call Center (Entry Point)
what_they_offer: Central phone line for anyone homeless or about to lose housing in suburban Cook County, including shelter referrals.
when_to_use: First call when someone is homeless or about to lose housing in suburban Cook County; after hours, use the 708-338-1724 x6 line.
who_is_eligible: People in suburban Cook County who are homeless or at risk of homelessness
hours: Mon-Fri 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; after hours 708-338-1724 x6 (Mon-Fri 4:30 p.m.-8:30 a.m., Sat-Sun 24 hours)
how_to_reach: 877-426-6515; https://myentrypoint.org/; https://www.housingforward.org/find-help
notes: Shelter referrals are by appointment only; "access to shelter is not guaranteed" (Entry Point).

what_they_offer: Drop-in center with showers, laundry, a mailing address, clothing, bag lunches, ID help and bilingual staff.
when_to_use: When someone experiencing homelessness needs a shower, laundry, clothes, a meal, a mailing address or ID help during the day.
who_is_eligible: Not published online; confirm: 708-338-1724
hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 9:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m.; Wed 9:00 a.m.-12:00 p.m.
how_to_reach: 1851 S. 9th Ave., Maywood (enter on Lexington); 708-338-1724; https://www.housingforward.org/find-help
notes: In Maywood, not Oak Park; transportation may be a barrier.

what_they_offer: A mobile outreach team finds people living outside and links them to case management and housing.
when_to_use: When you know someone living outside who may want help; email the outreach team.
who_is_eligible: People who are unsheltered in West Suburban Cook County
how_to_reach: Email outreachteam@housingforward.org to report someone who may need help; https://www.housingforward.org/services/respond
notes: No phone published for outreach requests; email only.

what_they_offer: Hotline for young people who have run away or are homeless.
when_to_use: When a young person has run away or is homeless and needs someone to talk to.
who_is_eligible: Young people who have run away or are homeless
how_to_reach: 1-800-RUNAWAY (1-800-786-2929); listed on the Village Street Outreach Card: https://www.oak-park.us/files/assets/oakpark/v/2/neighborhood-services/streetoutreachcards_oct-1.pdf
notes: Listed on the Village Street Outreach Card. Also listed under Youth/Family Services.

what_they_offer: Help with rent, utilities and other needs to avoid eviction.
when_to_use: When someone is behind on rent or utilities and at risk of eviction; start with the county call center.
who_is_eligible: People in suburban Cook County at risk of losing their housing; income rules not published online; confirm: 877-426-6515
how_to_reach: 877-426-6515 (Entry Point); https://www.housingforward.org/services/prevent; https://myentrypoint.org/

what_they_offer: Pays rent or mortgage, security deposits, move-in costs or utility bills directly to the landlord or provider.

cost: Assistance paid on your behalf; no fee published
notes: The FRAP page is not linked from the General Assistance page.

what_they_offer: Phone counseling for homeowners early in mortgage trouble, through a state (IHDA) hotline.

notes: The hotline is toll-free; the page does not say whether counseling is free.

notes: Police, fire and ER can refer; self-referral welcome.

when_to_use: When an adult living with mental illness wants peer support, social connection or help with work.
who_is_eligible: Adults 18+ living with a mental health condition
how_to_reach: 708-524-2582; 814 Harrison St., Oak Park, IL 60304; https://namimetsub.org/our-adult-programs/the-drop-in-center/
notes: Whether membership or registration is needed is not published; confirm 708-524-2582.

when_to_use: When someone needs ongoing therapy, medication management or trauma care, including uninsured Oak Park residents.

how_to_reach: 708-383-7500 (insurance questions ext. 2); access@thrivecc.org; 120 S. Marion St., Oak Park; https://thrivecc.org/
cost: Most Medicaid, most Medicare and many BCBS plans; sliding scale for uninsured with financial hardship; free for uninsured Oak Park residents
notes: Does not accept every plan (for example Humana Gold Plus Medicare).

what_they_offer: Residential treatment for adults and outpatient groups for adults and teens, plus a family group open to Oak Park residents.
when_to_use: When an adult or teen needs treatment for substance use or gambling, or a family member wants support.

cost: First 90 days of extended residential care free for new clients; free consultation; other costs and insurance not published, confirm 708-345-8422
notes: Reserved Oak Park beds may fill; ask about a waitlist. Website gives no street address.
